correctness.rationale: For every Haar-plane normal, the radial formula reduces the radius to the minimum \(\ell_1\) norm on the unit great circle. Positivity of the orthantwise sinusoidal norm excludes interior minima, leaving exact coordinate-zero candidates. The extreme absolute normal-coordinate pair maximizes the vertex radius by a signed derivative. Uniformity of the positive spherical octant and its six order chambers gives six congruent spherical triangles whose determinant and dot products yield the stated arctangent probability using the classical van Oosterom–Strackee formula. Endpoints, exceptional normals, no atoms, and the inverse CDF parameter are explicitly addressed. The standalone local checker validates 215 exact rational radius cases, spherical-excess geometry, Gaussian order-statistic quadrature, and finite sampled normals, but only the analytic proof establishes the universal claim.

value.rationale: The complete distribution of Haar-random central plane diameters of the canonical \(\ell_1^3\) ball is a mathematically natural exact random Gelfand-radius invariant. The result provides every tail probability, the sharp support, and an elementary closed arctangent expression rather than approximate asymptotic bounds. It forms a precise benchmark for the general recent probabilistic theory of section diameters and for the dual cube-projection inradius problem, without relying on hypothetical downstream theorems.
